items.title: The zeroth cohomology functor is right adjoint to the canonical functor out of the gluing category
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that in the gluing setup the functor H^0 from the gluing category Glue(R -> S, f_1, ..., f_t) to R-modules is right adjoint to the canonical functor Can in the other direction (source lines 24701-24707). The proof constructs the adjunction comparison map explicitly: for an object bold M = (M', M_i, alpha_i, alpha_ij) of the gluing category and an R-module N, the proof exhibits the map from Hom(Can(N), bold M) to Hom_R(N, H^0(bold M)) sending psi to H^0(psi) composed with the obvious map N -> H^0(Can(N)) (proof lines 24709-24718). It then notes that by construction this map is an isomorphism for N = R, even though R -> H^0(Can(R)) need not be an isomorphism in general (proof lines 24719-24720). The substantive step extends this from N = R to all N: the proof observes that the gluing category has direct sums and cokernels, that Can commutes with direct sums and cokernels, and hence that the displayed map is bijective because N can be written as a cokernel of a map between free R-modules (proof lines 24721-24724). The author states that the details are omitted (proof line 24725). The non-routine content is the reduction from the single case N = R to all modules by presenting N as a cokernel of free modules, using the exactness properties of Can.
